messages.content: use before in a request about washing hands and eating.
please wash your hands before eating.
now say that i already did it.
i washed my hands before eating.
why does the first use wash and the other washed?
the first asks someone to do the task. the other is about what you did before now, so washed is correct there.
can i say i wash my hands before eating if it is something i usually do?
yes. it can tell what you usually do, rather than what happened before one specific meal.
give that difference in two short sentences.
i wash my hands before eating can tell what you usually do. i washed my hands before eating can tell what you did before one meal.
now make it about my brother usually doing it.
my brother washes his hands before eating.
ask if he did it before this meal.
did my brother wash his hands before eating?
why wash after did, instead of washed?
did goes with wash in that question. use washed without did in the sentence my brother washed his hands.
i found the key i was looking for. i want to tell my friend, but not explain every place i looked.
i found the key i was looking for.
can you make it start with hello?
hello. i found the key i was looking for.
can you add where? it was under the book on my desk.
i found the key under the book on my desk.
does that mean i looked under the book first?
no. it gives where you found it, not the order of the places you looked in.
make that explanation shorter.
it says where the key was, not which places you looked in first.
now make it a message to my sister, who helped me look.
i found the key under the book on my desk. thank you for helping me look.
should i say she found it too?
only if she did. helping you look and being the person who found it are different parts of the task.
only give the short first sentence.
i found the key under the book on my desk.
write a story about someone being asked to meet at a place but not knowing where the journey starts. keep it simple.

a woman wanted to meet her brother at the market. he asked how long it would take to get there. she started to answer from her own house, then remembered that he was at the library. she asked which door he would leave from and whether he was walking. once she knew that, they could talk about the road from the library instead of the road from home. he left with a clear idea of where to go, and she knew when to begin her own walk. asking about the start had helped them make a plan for the real journey.
why was her first idea not enough?
she was thinking about the way from her house. he needed the way from the library.
did the market change place?
no. the starting place was different, so the journey to the same market could be different.
what could she ask before giving a time?
where are you starting from, and are you walking?
can you know the number of minutes from this story?
no. it does not say how far the market is from the library or how long he took to walk.
only give the part about what is not known.
we do not know how far it is or how long the walk took.
finish with them meeting without adding a number.
he came to the market as she came along the road from home. they met near the door and went inside together.
i listened to music for six minutes. for the last two minutes, i also drew a picture. how many minutes did i draw?
you drew for two minutes.
how long was it from starting the music to finishing the drawing?
six minutes, if you finished drawing when you stopped listening to the music.
explain why that is the answer.
the drawing took place during the music. if they finished together, the whole time was the six minutes of music.
that is what happened. did music and drawing together take eight minutes on the clock?
no. the drawing happened during the last two minutes of the music, so the clock time was six minutes.
how much music time had no drawing?
four minutes.
now i draw for one more minute after the music stops.
then you drew for three minutes in all, and seven minutes went by from starting the music to finishing the drawing.
why not add all the music and all the drawing for clock time?
you listened and drew together for two minutes. those two minutes happened once on the clock, even though you did two things.
make that explanation shorter.
two minutes had both things happening, so do not add those minutes again for the clock time.
there is a small room in the library i like. it has a table near the window, and i can read there quietly.
what do you like most about reading there?
i like that it is not my work desk. when i sit there, i feel like the book can be the whole task.
the change of place helps you give that time to the book, rather than the other work you know from your desk.
yes. i do not need the room to be important to anyone else. it just helps me read.
you can like the room for that simple use. it does not need to be a place that everyone would choose.
write one sentence about why i like it.
i like the small library room because i can sit by the window and let reading be my whole task for a while.
can you make it shorter?
i like having a quiet place where reading is the whole task.
does that say i hate my work desk?
no. you can like another place for reading without saying you hate your desk.
now only give a kind reply without a question.
it sounds like you have found a place that helps you enjoy your book.
is more water the same as another cup?
not always. more water asks for water. another cup asks for one more cup or a different cup. the context helps us know which.
give that difference more simply.
more water is about the water. another cup is about the cup.
i have a cup already and only want more water in it.
then you could ask: could i have more water in this cup, please?
only give that request without the explanation.
could i have more water in this cup, please?
now i want an empty cup for my friend.
could i have another empty cup for my friend, please?
why empty?
you said you wanted an empty cup. keeping that word helps make clear that the request is for a cup, not a drink already in it.
now ask for more tea but keep the same cup.
could i have more tea in this cup, please?
can you know whether there is already tea left in it?
not from the request alone. you have not said whether the cup is empty or still has some tea.
write a story about a child who knows the way to the school but not all the way to the market. the child should not make up the rest.

a child was walking with his aunt when she asked whether he knew the way to the market. he said he knew the road as far as the school, but had not gone from there to the market alone. they walked that part together. near the school, his aunt showed him where the road turned to go to the market. he looked at the place and asked what he should remember for the way back. she showed him a large tree and the school door. he had helped with what he knew and learned a new part without saying he had known the whole journey from the start.
why was his answer useful even though it was not the whole way?
it told his aunt which part he knew. she could use that information and help with the part he did not know.
what would have been wrong with saying i know the whole way?
it would give her a false idea about what he knew. she might then not explain the new part.
use words without false.
it would make her think he knew more than he did. she might not explain the part he needed.
write his first answer in his voice.
i know the way to the school, but not the whole way to the market.
what did he ask about the return?
he asked what he should remember for the way back.
finish with him drawing the new part later.
at home, he drew the school, the tree, and the road to the market on a page. he told his aunt which part he had learned that day.
my friend only wrote okay. can you know they are sad?
no. okay is a short reply, but it does not tell us their whole feeling without more context.
they usually write more. does that tell you for sure something is wrong?
no. a different reply does not tell us the reason by itself. they could be busy, tired, or simply giving a short answer.
make that explanation shorter.
the reply is shorter than you usually get, but that does not tell us why.
can i ask without saying they are sad?
yes. you could say: is this a good time to talk, or would another time be better?
what if i only need to know whether they saw my plan?
then ask that specific question. did you see the time and place in my message?
write it as one short message.
did you see the time and place i sent?
why is that useful for my plan?
it asks for the information you need for the plan. the short reply alone does not tell you every feeling your friend has.
say that in fewer words.
the question asks about the plan. okay alone does not tell you every feeling they have.
